text:
marcus: Putting up a tiny docs PR to add a 'compatibility matrix' snippet generator for model cards. Idea: a one-line table that authors can paste that shows streaming/embeds/longctx/quant-support. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3012

anya: neat. Will it be a small JS snippet that authors can run? or a copy-paste table?

marcus: both. It'll generate a markdown table from a JSON manifest. Also adding a short README on how to update the manifest when adding new variants.

frank: please ensure the matrix rows are per-variant not per-model-family. We had confusion previously. Also include a 'notes' column for quirks.

bench-bot: automated bench scan attached  flagging orion-quant-variants: streaming false, embed true, longctx limited. See gist in PR comments.

docs-bot: PR opened by marcus in redwood-inference/docs (#3012)  labels: docs, tooling

marcus: pushing a tiny example usage in the PR description. Asking docs reviewers to sanity-check phrasing.

anya: thumbs up. This should reduce repeated prose across cards. Add a link to the canonical model-catalog page in the README so authors know where to cross-reference.

frank: small editorial nit: call out that the matrix generator is intended for internal docs authors only and not the public API docs; we don't want to promise compatibility guarantees to customers in a generated table without audits.

marcus: noted, added an internal-only banner in the README and a link to the audit checklist.

anya: adding to my review queue. will review after lunch.

frank: thanks — if this lands, we should run a follow-up pass to convert existing cards to use the generated matrix to standardize phrasing.

marcus: agreed, planning a migration script after landing. will open a follow-up GH issue.
